_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §FX] The real Earth as the planet (design 18 Oct §FX, Mike: 'lock it in'). Three rasters, all equirectangular (row 0 is the north edge at +90°, column 0 the −180° edge, sample centres at the half-step), built from public sources by Claude Code's build script (queue 103–105) and committed small; the sources themselves (hundreds of MB each) live outside the repo and are gitignored. The planet's size, heights and time are unchanged: world_scale.json (1/100 sideways, 1/10 up, the 144-minute day). First guesses by Claude (chat), 18 Oct; the designer owns them. Reference maths: tools/reference/earth_reference.py. Validator: tools/earth_data_check.py.
_help.on: true: TerrainField, climate_pass, RealmMap and biome_pass read the rasters below (§FX.3–5). false: the noise planet as built on 3 Oct (§CR), for comparison. The dev postage stamp (STAMP=1) is always the noise planet.
_help.relief: §FX.3. file: int16 Earth metres, 'width' × 'height' samples (10 arc-minutes: 2,160 × 1,080, about 4.7 MB raw). The game multiplies by world_scale.json → heights.height_scale (0.1). Below sea_level_m is sea; land below sea level (the Dead Sea, Death Valley) stays land and the hydrology pass fills closed basins. format: 'int16_le_raw' (relief.bin) or 'png16' (relief.png); Claude Code records which. source_grid is the ETOPO product averaged (60 arc-second ice surface). min_m, max_m and built are filled by the build script. The 10' average shaves the sharpest summits (§FX.3): the highest cell here is expected at 600–700 m, not 885.
_help.sea_level_m: Sea level in the map's metres. 0 is ETOPO's; a positive value floods, a negative one drains (a cheap way to see a lower sea).
_help.blueprint_sampling: How the 1 km blueprint reads the map: 'footprint_mean' averages all samples under a cell (the design's choice, §FX.3: climate and rivers see the smoothed relief); 'centre' takes one bilinear sample (aliases). The walking-scale chunks always sample bilinear and add the detail layers.
_help.ranges: §FX.3, §CR.4. stretch_max: 1.0 is the honest map (this pass). Above 1.0, the great ranges (regions above route_region_min_m here) are exaggerated sideways up to this factor, the lowland around them squeezed to pay for it, so routes at or under world_scale.json → mountains.route_max_deg exist (§FX.10 call 4; not built unless Mike asks after queue 106's report). route_region_min_m and lowland_max_m are the route check's thresholds (queue 106), in this world's metres.
_help.peaks: §FX.3, §FX.10 call 5. The named summits with their true coordinates and heights in Earth metres (Wikipedia / national surveys, rounded). restore_named false: nothing is stamped; queue 103's check reports how far below each the averaged cell sits. true: each is stamped back at walking scale at its coordinates at its height × height_scale, a spike inside its cell (not built).
_help.climate: §FX.4. CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981–2010 (Karger et al. 2017; CC0), block-averaged to 0.25° (1,440 × 720), int16. units: what each file holds after Claude Code's conversion (read CHELSA's technical documentation for each source file's scale and offset and record them in 'source_scale_offset'). CHELSA is land-only: sea_fill says what the sea samples hold ('nearest_land': the nearest land value; 'none': 0 and the simulation's own). The climate pass reads bio1 (mean annual temperature) and bio12 (annual precipitation) as the long-term climate; bio5 − bio6 sizes the seasons' swing; bio15 is kept for the weather simulation's rain seasonality. Fallback if the downloads are a problem: WorldClim 2.1 at 10' is 3 MB, but its site states no terms (Mike's call before anything ships).
_help.ecoregions: §FX.5. RESOLVE Ecoregions 2017 (Dinerstein et al. 2017; CC BY 4.0): 846 terrestrial ecoregions in 14 biomes and 8 realms. file: uint16 ECO_ID per sample at 0.1° (3,600 × 1,800), 0 where there is none (sea); 0.25° if it will not compress under about 3 MB. table: the attribute export (ECO_ID → ECO_NAME, BIOME_NUM, BIOME_NAME, REALM). realms: the rules that give each ecoregion one game realm (realms.json), resolved into resolved_realms by tools/earth_data_check.py --ecoregions --write. biome_map: which game templates each RESOLVE biome may be (biome_map.json). An id is never interpolated: nearest sample; a land cell with 0 takes the nearest non-zero within nearest_fill_cells blueprint cells.
_help.credits: Shown wherever the game shows credits (queue 103 decides where). RESOLVE's CC BY 4.0 requires its line; the others are courtesy.
_help.checks: Known places for the headless checks (queue 103–105), latitude then longitude in degrees, with the numbers to expect. bio1 in °C, bio12 in mm a year; relief in Earth metres before height_scale; biome is the template the cell is expected to get, realm the game realm. Tolerances: temperature ±2 °C, precipitation ±25%, position within one blueprint cell.

relief.source: ETOPO 2022 Global Relief Model, ice surface, 60 arc-second (NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, 2022; doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74)

climate.source: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981–2010, 30 arc-second (Karger, D.N. et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122; CC0 1.0)

units.bio5: 0.1 degC (mean daily maximum of the warmest month)
units.bio6: 0.1 degC (mean daily minimum of the coldest month)

ecoregions.source: RESOLVE Ecoregions 2017 (Dinerstein, E. et al. 2017, BioScience 67(6):534–545; CC BY 4.0; ecoregions2017.appspot.com)
